scope.title: Master Public Health Indicator Registry
scope.boundary: All catalogue records satisfying the published inclusion rule for each Release 1 source, plus the curated priority collection.

whoBuildingBlocks.framework: WHO Monitoring the Building Blocks of Health Systems
whoBuildingBlocks.method: Deterministic multi-label analytical classification using domains and indicator metadata; mappings are discovery aids, not source-custodian classifications.

coverage.definition: All catalogue records satisfying the published inclusion rule for each Release 1 source, plus the curated priority collection.
coverage.statement: Bounded-exhaustive for the four declared machine-readable/global catalogues at the cut-off date. It is not yet exhaustive across every authority in the source census.
coverage.indiaStatus: No India-source-specific records in Release 1; authoritative programme sources are now scheduled for phased extraction.

sources.access: IHIP portal, surveillance reports and forms

indicators.name: Life expectancy at birth
indicators.definition: Expected years a newborn would live if current age- and sex-specific mortality rates continued.
indicators.dataSource: Complete civil registration and population estimates
indicators.uses: Population health surveillance; trend analysis; inequality assessment; planning
indicators.caveats: Sensitive to mortality data completeness; period measure, not a forecast
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Healthy life expectancy at birth (HALE)
indicators.definition: Expected years lived in full health after accounting for time lived with disease or injury.
indicators.numerator: Life-table person-years adjusted for health-state severity
indicators.dataSource: Mortality data plus morbidity, disability weights and models
indicators.uses: Burden assessment; cross-population comparison; priority setting
indicators.caveats: Model-dependent; uncertainty and disability weights must accompany comparisons
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Disability-adjusted life years (DALYs)
indicators.definition: Healthy years lost from premature mortality and non-fatal health loss.
indicators.numerator: Years of life lost + years lived with disability
indicators.formula: YLL + YLD; often reported as count or rate
indicators.dataSource: Cause-of-death data, epidemiological studies and burden models
indicators.uses: Burden estimation; priority setting; economic evaluation; research
indicators.caveats: Comparability depends on methods, disability weights and uncertainty intervals
indicators.source: Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation — curated authoritative source
indicators.org: Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Under-five mortality rate
indicators.definition: Probability per 1,000 live births that a newborn dies before age five under current mortality conditions.
indicators.numerator: Deaths before age five represented through life-table methods
indicators.formula: Probability of dying before age five × 1,000
indicators.dataSource: CRVS; census; household surveys; modelled estimates
indicators.uses: Child survival surveillance; planning; SDG reporting; equity analysis
indicators.caveats: Not simply deaths divided by births when life-table estimation is used
indicators.source: UN IGME / UNICEF — curated authoritative source
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Neonatal mortality rate
indicators.definition: Probability per 1,000 live births that a newborn dies during the first 28 completed days.
indicators.uses: Newborn surveillance; maternal-newborn programme evaluation; SDG reporting
indicators.caveats: Early neonatal deaths may be misclassified as stillbirths
indicators.source: UN IGME / UNICEF — curated authoritative source
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Maternal mortality ratio
indicators.definition: Maternal deaths during a period per 100,000 live births in the same period.
indicators.population: Women during pregnancy, childbirth or within the specified postpartum period
indicators.dataSource: CRVS with cause of death; confidential enquiry; surveys; models
indicators.disaggregation: Age; residence; socioeconomic position where stable
indicators.uses: Maternal health surveillance; quality improvement; SDG reporting
indicators.caveats: Rare event; under-identification and pregnancy-status ascertainment affect estimates
indicators.source: WHO and UN Maternal Mortality Estimation Inter-Agency Group — curated authoritative source
indicators.org: WHO and UN Maternal Mortality Estimation Inter-Agency Group
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Premature mortality from major NCDs
indicators.definition: Unconditional probability of dying between ages 30 and 70 from cardiovascular disease, cancer, diabetes or chronic respiratory disease.
indicators.numerator: Life-table deaths from four NCD groups ages 30–70
indicators.denominator: Population exposed through cause-specific life table
indicators.dataSource: CRVS cause-of-death data and population estimates
indicators.uses: NCD surveillance; policy evaluation; international comparison
indicators.caveats: Requires comparable ICD coding and adequate cause-of-death completeness
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Suicide mortality rate
indicators.definition: Deaths due to suicide per 100,000 population in a defined period.
indicators.disaggregation: Age; sex; geography; method where permitted
indicators.uses: Mental health surveillance; prevention planning; inequality analysis
indicators.caveats: Intent may be misclassified; small-area rates can be unstable
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Road traffic injury death rate
indicators.definition: Deaths caused by road traffic injuries per 100,000 population.
indicators.dataSource: CRVS; police records; health records; modelling
indicators.uses: Road-safety surveillance; policy evaluation; geographic comparison
indicators.caveats: Police and health sources differ; delayed deaths and under-reporting matter
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: HIV incidence rate
indicators.definition: New HIV infections during the period per 1,000 people at risk of acquiring HIV.
indicators.dataSource: Surveillance, surveys, programme data and epidemiological models
indicators.uses: Epidemic surveillance; prevention evaluation; SDG reporting
indicators.caveats: Often model-derived; key-population denominators can be uncertain
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Tuberculosis incidence rate
indicators.definition: Estimated new and relapse TB episodes arising in a year per 100,000 population.
indicators.dataSource: TB surveillance, notifications, prevalence surveys and models
indicators.uses: TB burden assessment; programme planning; SDG reporting
indicators.caveats: Notification rate is not incidence where detection is incomplete
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Malaria incidence rate
indicators.definition: New malaria cases per 1,000 population at risk during a year.
indicators.uses: Malaria surveillance; intervention targeting; SDG reporting
indicators.caveats: Testing practice, care seeking and risk-population estimation affect rates
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Hepatitis B surface antigen prevalence in children
indicators.definition: Percentage of tested children in the defined age group positive for hepatitis B surface antigen.
indicators.uses: Transmission monitoring; immunization programme evaluation
indicators.caveats: Assay, age group and survey representativeness must match
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Cancer incidence rate by site
indicators.definition: New primary cancers diagnosed in a defined population and period, usually age-standardized.
indicators.formula: Cases / population × 100,000; direct age standardization where specified
indicators.disaggregation: Age; sex; cancer site; stage; geography
indicators.uses: Cancer surveillance; service planning; prevention evaluation
indicators.caveats: Registry completeness, multiple-primary rules and standard population affect comparisons
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Cholera case fatality ratio
indicators.definition: Percentage of reported cholera cases who die from cholera in the reporting period.
indicators.uses: Outbreak severity monitoring; care quality; emergency response
indicators.caveats: Case definition, under-ascertainment and community deaths can bias the ratio
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Adolescent birth rate
indicators.definition: Live births to girls or women in a specified adolescent age group per 1,000 females in that group.
indicators.denominator: Females/person-years in the same age group
indicators.disaggregation: Age group; education; residence; marital status; wealth
indicators.uses: Adolescent health surveillance; reproductive health planning; equity analysis
indicators.caveats: Survey and CRVS reference periods differ; births under age 15 are often sparse
indicators.source: UN DESA / UNFPA — curated authoritative source
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Child stunting prevalence
indicators.definition: Percentage of children under five with height-for-age below −2 SD of the WHO Child Growth Standards median.
indicators.numerator: Children under five with HAZ < −2 SD
indicators.denominator: Children under five measured with valid anthropometry
indicators.disaggregation: Age; sex; residence; wealth; maternal education
indicators.uses: Nutrition surveillance; programme targeting; SDG reporting
indicators.caveats: Anthropometric measurement error and exclusion rules affect estimates
indicators.source: UNICEF / WHO / World Bank — curated authoritative source
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Child wasting prevalence
indicators.definition: Percentage of children under five with weight-for-height below −2 SD of WHO standards.
indicators.numerator: Children under five with WHZ < −2 SD
indicators.denominator: Children under five measured with valid anthropometry
indicators.uses: Acute malnutrition assessment; humanitarian planning; SDG reporting
indicators.caveats: Strong seasonality; oedema and anthropometric quality must be handled consistently
indicators.source: UNICEF / WHO / World Bank — curated authoritative source
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Child overweight prevalence
indicators.definition: Percentage of children under five with weight-for-height above +2 SD of WHO standards.
indicators.numerator: Children under five with WHZ > +2 SD
indicators.denominator: Children under five measured with valid anthropometry
indicators.uses: Double-burden surveillance; prevention planning; SDG reporting
indicators.caveats: Anthropometric quality and biologically implausible value rules matter
indicators.source: UNICEF / WHO / World Bank — curated authoritative source
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Exclusive breastfeeding under six months
indicators.definition: Percentage of infants 0–5 months who received only breast milk during the previous day, with standard exceptions.
indicators.numerator: Infants 0–5 months exclusively breastfed in prior 24 hours
indicators.dataSource: DHS, MICS or equivalent household survey
indicators.disaggregation: Age in months; sex; residence; wealth; maternal education
indicators.uses: Infant feeding monitoring; programme evaluation; advocacy
indicators.caveats: 24-hour recall can overstate sustained exclusive breastfeeding
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Low birthweight prevalence
indicators.definition: Percentage of liveborn infants weighing less than 2,500 grams at birth.
indicators.dataSource: Facility records, birth registration and household surveys
indicators.uses: Maternal-newborn surveillance; nutrition planning
indicators.caveats: Missing and heaped birthweights; facility data may not represent all births
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Anaemia prevalence in women aged 15–49
indicators.definition: Percentage of non-pregnant or pregnant women aged 15–49 below the applicable haemoglobin threshold after recommended adjustments.
indicators.uses: Micronutrient surveillance; programme planning; SDG reporting
indicators.caveats: Altitude, smoking, pregnancy and measurement method require standard adjustment
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Population using safely managed drinking-water services
indicators.definition: Percentage using an improved drinking-water source located on premises, available when needed and free from priority contamination.
indicators.numerator: Population meeting all safely managed water criteria
indicators.dataSource: Censuses, household surveys, regulators and administrative sources
indicators.uses: WASH surveillance; infrastructure planning; equity analysis; SDG reporting
indicators.caveats: Water quality and availability data are often missing; national definitions vary
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Population using safely managed sanitation services
indicators.definition: Percentage using improved sanitation not shared with other households, with excreta safely disposed in situ or transported and treated off-site.
indicators.numerator: Population meeting safely managed sanitation criteria
indicators.dataSource: Censuses, household surveys and administrative sources
indicators.uses: WASH surveillance; infrastructure planning; SDG reporting
indicators.caveats: Faecal-sludge management evidence is incomplete in many settings
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Population with a basic handwashing facility
indicators.definition: Percentage living in households with a handwashing facility on premises with soap and water observed.
indicators.numerator: Population in households with observed soap and water facility
indicators.uses: Hygiene planning; infectious disease prevention; SDG reporting
indicators.caveats: Observation is point-in-time and does not measure actual handwashing behaviour
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Primary reliance on clean fuels and technologies
indicators.definition: Percentage primarily relying on fuels and technologies classified as clean for cooking, heating or lighting under the relevant definition.
indicators.numerator: Population relying primarily on clean fuels/technology
indicators.dataSource: Household surveys, censuses and energy statistics
indicators.uses: Energy-health planning; exposure surveillance; SDG reporting
indicators.caveats: Primary fuel may miss fuel stacking; classifications and end uses must match
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Population-weighted annual mean PM2.5 exposure
indicators.definition: Annual mean concentration of fine particulate matter weighted by the population distribution.
indicators.dataSource: Ground monitors, satellite observations and atmospheric models
indicators.uses: Air-quality surveillance; burden assessment; policy evaluation
indicators.caveats: Model resolution, sparse monitors and exposure misclassification affect local use
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Current tobacco use prevalence age 15+
indicators.definition: Age-standardized percentage of people aged 15+ currently using smoked or smokeless tobacco, daily or non-daily, according to the series definition.
indicators.disaggregation: Age; sex; residence; wealth; product type
indicators.uses: Risk-factor surveillance; policy evaluation; SDG reporting
indicators.caveats: Question wording, product coverage and age standardization must match
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Alcohol per capita consumption age 15+
indicators.definition: Litres of pure alcohol consumed per person aged 15+ in a year, combining recorded and estimated unrecorded consumption and adjusting for tourism where applicable.
indicators.numerator: Total litres of pure alcohol consumed
indicators.unit: Litres of pure alcohol per person aged 15+
indicators.dataSource: Sales, production, tax, survey and tourism data
indicators.disaggregation: Sex only through separate consumption measures; geography where available
indicators.uses: Alcohol policy monitoring; burden modelling; SDG reporting
indicators.caveats: Population average hides distribution; unrecorded consumption is modelled
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Raised blood pressure prevalence in adults
indicators.definition: Percentage of adults meeting the specified systolic/diastolic threshold or taking antihypertensive medication, with age standardization where stated.
indicators.numerator: Adults meeting threshold or treatment criterion
indicators.disaggregation: Age; sex; residence; wealth; treatment status
indicators.uses: NCD risk surveillance; treatment planning; equity analysis
indicators.caveats: Threshold, medication inclusion, measurement protocol and age range must match
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Adult obesity prevalence
indicators.definition: Percentage of adults with body mass index at or above 30 kg/m² under the stated age and measurement definition.
indicators.dataSource: Measured health examination survey; self-report only with caution
indicators.uses: NCD surveillance; prevention planning; evaluation
indicators.caveats: Self-report bias; pregnancy exclusions and age standardization must match
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Diabetes or raised blood glucose prevalence
indicators.definition: Percentage of adults meeting the specified glucose/HbA1c criterion or taking diabetes medication.
indicators.numerator: Adults meeting biomarker or medication criterion
indicators.uses: Diabetes surveillance; service planning; equity analysis
indicators.caveats: Fasting status, biomarker, threshold and medication inclusion must match
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Insufficient physical activity prevalence
indicators.definition: Percentage not meeting the applicable WHO physical-activity recommendation for age.
indicators.uses: Risk-factor surveillance; health promotion planning
indicators.caveats: Questionnaire domains, devices and recommendation versions are not interchangeable
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Intimate partner violence prevalence
indicators.definition: Percentage of ever-partnered women and girls in the specified age range experiencing physical, sexual or psychological violence by a current or former partner during the reference period.
indicators.population: Ever-partnered women and girls in defined age range
indicators.disaggregation: Age; type of violence; residence; wealth; disability
indicators.uses: Violence prevention; service planning; equity analysis; SDG reporting
indicators.caveats: Safety, disclosure, reference period and instrument strongly affect estimates
indicators.source: UN Women / WHO / UNICEF / UNSD — curated authoritative source
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Demand for family planning satisfied with modern methods
indicators.definition: Percentage of women of reproductive age needing contraception whose need is met using a modern method.
indicators.numerator: Women needing contraception who use a modern method
indicators.population: Women aged 15–49, according to source definition
indicators.dataSource: DHS, MICS, reproductive health surveys and routine data with caution
indicators.disaggregation: Age; marital status; residence; wealth; parity
indicators.uses: Family-planning monitoring; equity analysis; SDG reporting
indicators.caveats: Definitions of need, sexual activity and modern methods must be preserved
indicators.source: UN DESA Population Division — curated authoritative source
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Antenatal care coverage—four or more contacts
indicators.definition: Percentage of women with a recent live birth who received antenatal care at least four times during pregnancy.
indicators.numerator: Women with recent live birth reporting ≥4 ANC contacts
indicators.denominator: Women with a recent live birth
indicators.population: Women aged 15–49 with a recent live birth
indicators.dataSource: Household surveys; validated routine information systems
indicators.uses: Maternal programme monitoring; UHC assessment; equity analysis
indicators.caveats: Contact count does not measure timing or quality; WHO now recommends eight contacts
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Births attended by skilled health personnel
indicators.definition: Percentage of live births attended by personnel competent in maternal and newborn care under the current definition.
indicators.numerator: Live births attended by skilled personnel
indicators.disaggregation: Residence; wealth; maternal age; education; place of birth
indicators.uses: Maternal-newborn monitoring; workforce planning; SDG reporting
indicators.caveats: Professional titles do not guarantee competence; quality and referral capacity are not captured
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Postnatal care coverage for mothers and newborns
indicators.definition: Percentage receiving a postnatal health check within the specified time after birth, reported separately for mother and newborn.
indicators.numerator: Eligible mothers/newborns receiving timely postnatal check
indicators.population: Women with recent birth and liveborn newborns
indicators.dataSource: Household surveys and routine maternal-newborn systems
indicators.disaggregation: Residence; wealth; age; place of birth
indicators.uses: Postnatal programme monitoring; equity analysis
indicators.caveats: Timing and content definitions vary; mother and newborn should not be merged
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: DTP3 immunization coverage
indicators.definition: Percentage of the target infant cohort receiving three doses of diphtheria-tetanus-pertussis-containing vaccine.
indicators.numerator: Target children receiving DTP-containing vaccine dose 3
indicators.dataSource: Administrative coverage, surveys and WHO/UNICEF estimation
indicators.disaggregation: Sex where available; geography; wealth from surveys
indicators.uses: Immunization monitoring; zero-dose/dropout analysis; UHC assessment
indicators.caveats: Denominator error and undocumented doses can yield implausible administrative coverage
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: Measles second-dose immunization coverage
indicators.definition: Percentage of the nationally defined target cohort receiving a second measles-containing vaccine dose.
indicators.dataSource: Administrative coverage, surveys and WHO/UNICEF estimation
indicators.disaggregation: Sex where available; geography; wealth from surveys
indicators.uses: Immunization monitoring; outbreak-risk assessment
indicators.caveats: Target age and schedule vary by country; administrative denominators may be weak
indicators.whoPillarBasis: Rule-based analytical mapping to the WHO health-system building-block framework; not assigned by the source custodian.

indicators.name: HPV vaccine coverage in primary target cohort
indicators.definition: Percentage of the nationally defined primary target cohort receiving the final recommended HPV vaccine dose.
indicators.numerator: People in target cohort receiving final recommended dose

indicators.name: People using at least basic drinking water services, rural (% of rural population)
indicators.definition: The percentage of people using at least basic water services. This indicator encompasses both people using basic water services as well as those using safely managed water services. Basic drinking water services is defined as drinking water from an improved source, provided collection time is not more than 30 minutes for a round trip. Improved water sources include piped water, boreholes or tubewells, protected dug wells, protected springs, and packaged or delivered water.

indicators.name: Prevalence of current tobacco use (% of adults)

indicators.name: Mortality rate attributed to household and ambient air pollution, age-standardized, male (per 100,000 male population)
indicators.definition: Mortality rate attributed to household and ambient air pollution is the number of deaths attributable to the joint effects of household and ambient air pollution in a year per 100,000 population. The rates are age-standardized. Following diseases are taken into account: acute respiratory infections (estimated for all ages); cerebrovascular diseases in adults (estimated above 25 years); ischaemic heart diseases in adults (estimated above 25 years); chronic obstructive pulmonary disease in adults (estimated above 25 years); and lung cancer in adults (estimated above 25 years).

indicators.name: People using at least basic sanitation services, rural (% of rural population)
indicators.definition: The percentage of people using at least basic sanitation services, that is, improved sanitation facilities that are not shared with other households. This indicator encompasses both people using basic sanitation services as well as those using safely managed sanitation services. Improved sanitation facilities include flush/pour flush to piped sewer systems, septic tanks or pit latrines; ventilated improved pit latrines, composting toilets or pit latrines with slabs.

Each index is expressed in terms of the number of standard deviation (SD) units from the median of the WHO Child Growth Standards. Children are classified as malnourished if their z-scores are below minus two or minus three standard deviations (-2 SD or -3 SD) from the median of the WHO Child Growth Standards. The percentage below -2 SD includes children who are below -3 SD.
indicators.uses: Discovery; indicator selection; cross-registry comparison; source metadata retrieval

indicators.name: Maternal mortality ratio (modeled estimate, per 100,000 live births)
indicators.definition: Maternal mortality ratio is the number of women who die from pregnancy-related causes while pregnant or within 42 days of pregnancy termination per 100,000 live births. The data are estimated with a regression model using information on the proportion of maternal deaths among non-AIDS deaths in women ages 15-49, fertility, birth attendants, and GDP measured using purchasing power parities (PPPs).

indicators.name: Malnourished children (stunting, -3SD) (% of children under 5): Q1 (lowest)

Each index is expressed in terms of the number of standard deviation (SD) units from the median of the WHO Child Growth Standards. Children are classified as malnourished if their z-scores are below minus two or minus three standard deviations (-2 SD or -3 SD) from the median of the WHO Child Growth Standards. The percentage below -2 SD includes children who are below -3 SD.

indicators.name: Proportion of population pushed further below the $2.15 ($ 2017 PPP) poverty line by out-of-pocket health care expenditure (%)
indicators.domain: Health services and universal health coverage
indicators.definition: This indicator shows the fraction of a country’s population living in households whose non-health expenditures are already below the $2.15 poverty line and who as a result are pushed further into poverty by their out-of-pocket health spending. Out-of-pocket health expenditure is defined as any spending incurred by a household when any member uses a health good or service to receive any type of care (preventive, curative, rehabilitative, long-term or palliative care); provided by any type of provider; for any type of disease, illness or health condition; in any type of setting (outpatient, inpatient, at home).

indicators.name: Increase in poverty gap at $1.90 ($ 2011 PPP) poverty line due to out-of-pocket health care expenditure (USD)
indicators.domain: Health services and universal health coverage
indicators.definition: Increase in poverty gap at $1.90 ($ 2011 PPP) poverty line due to out-of-pocket health care expenditure, expressed in US dollars (2011 PPP). The poverty gap increase due to out-of-pocket health spending is one way to measure how much out-of-pocket health spending pushes people below or further below the poverty line (the difference in the poverty gap due to out-of-pocket health spending being included or excluded from the measure of household welfare). This difference corresponds to the total out-of-pocket health spending for households that are already below the poverty line, to the amount that exceeds the shortfall between the poverty line and total consumption for households that are impoverished by out-of-pocket health spending and to zero for households whose consumption is above the poverty line after accounting for out-of-pocket health spending.
indicators.dataSource: World Health Organization and World Bank. 2019. Global Monitoring Report on Financial Protection in Health 2019. NOTE: This indicator has been discontinued as of December 2021. indicators.name: Proportion of population pushed below the $2.15 ($ 2017 PPP) poverty line by out-of-pocket health care expenditure (%)
indicators.domain: Health services and universal health coverage
indicators.definition: This indicator shows the fraction of a country’s population experiencing out-of-pocket health impoverishing expenditures, defined as expenditures without which the household they live in would have been above the $ 2.15 poverty line, but because of the expenditures is below the poverty line. Out-of-pocket health expenditure is defined as any spending incurred by a household when any member uses a health good or service to receive any type of care (preventive, curative, rehabilitative, long-term or palliative care); provided by any type of provider; for any type of disease, illness or health condition; in any type of setting (outpatient, inpatient, at home).

indicators.name: Increase in poverty gap at $3.20 ($ 2011 PPP) poverty line due to out-of-pocket health care expenditure (USD)
indicators.domain: Health services and universal health coverage
indicators.definition: Increase in poverty gap at $3.20 ($ 2011 PPP) poverty line due to out-of-pocket health care expenditure, expressed in US dollars (2011 PPP). The poverty gap increase due to out-of-pocket health spending is one way to measure how much out-of-pocket health spending pushes people below or further below the poverty line (the difference in the poverty gap due to out-of-pocket health spending being included or excluded from the measure of household welfare). This difference corresponds to the total out-of-pocket health spending for households that are already below the poverty line, to the amount that exceeds the shortfall between the poverty line and total consumption for households that are impoverished by out-of-pocket health spending and to zero for households whose consumption is above the poverty line after accounting for out-of-pocket health spending.

indicators.name: Refugee population by country or territory of asylum
indicators.definition: Refugees are people who are recognized as refugees under the 1951 Convention Relating to the Status of Refugees or its 1967 Protocol, the 1969 Organization of African Unity Convention Governing the Specific Aspects of Refugee Problems in Africa, people recognized as refugees in accordance with the UNHCR statute, people granted refugee-like humanitarian status, and people provided temporary protection. Asylum seekers--people who have applied for asylum or refugee status and who have not yet received a decision or who are registered as asylum seekers--are excluded. Palestinian refugees are people (and their descendants) whose residence was Palestine between June 1946 and May 1948 and who lost their homes and means of livelihood as a result of the 1948 Arab-Israeli conflict. Country of asylum is the country where an asylum claim was filed and granted.
indicators.dataSource: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) and UNRWA through UNHCR's Refugee Data Finder at https://www.unhcr.org/refugee-statistics/.

indicators.name: Depth of the food deficit (kilocalories per person per day)
indicators.definition: The depth of the food deficit indicates how many calories would be needed to lift the undernourished from their status, everything else being constant. The average intensity of food deprivation of the undernourished, estimated as the difference between the average dietary energy requirement and the average dietary energy consumption of the undernourished population (food-deprived), is multiplied by the number of undernourished to provide an estimate of the total food deficit in the country, which is then normalized by the total population.

indicators.name: Depth of hunger (kilocalories per person per day)
indicators.definition: Depth of hunger or the intensity of food deprivation, indicates how much food-deprived people fall short of minimum food needs in terms of dietary energy. The food deficit, in kilocalories per person per day, is measured by comparing the average amount of dietary energy that undernourished people get from the foods they eat with the minimum amount of dietary energy they need to maintain body weight and undertake light activity. The depth of hunger is low when it is less than 200 kilocalories per person per day, and high when it is higher than 300 kilocalories per person per day.
indicators.dataSource: Food and Agriculture Organization, Food Security Statistics (http://www.fao.org/economic/ess/food-security-statistics/en/).

Unmet need for spacing includes pregnant women whose pregnancy was mistimed, amenorrheic women who are not using family planning and whose last birth was mistimed, and fecund women who are neither pregnant nor amenorrheic and who are not using any method of family planning and say they want to wait 2 or more years for their next birth. Also included in unmet need for spacing are fecund women who are not using any method of family planning and say they are unsure whether they want another child or who want another child but are unsure when to have the birth unless they say it would not be a problem if they discovered they were pregnant in the next few weeks. Unmet need for limiting refers to pregnant women whose pregnancy was unwanted, amenorrheic women whose last child was unwanted, and fecund women who are neither pregnant nor amenorrheic and who are not using any method of family planning and who want no more children. Excluded from the unmet need category are pregnant and amenorrheic women who became pregnant while using a method (these women are in need of a better method of contraception).

indicators.caveats: This is a source-specific catalogue manifestation. Do not assume equivalence with similarly named records until a methodological crosswalk is validated.

indicators.name: Refugees
indicators.definition: Persons who have current refugee status, granted either before arrival or upon arrival in the receiving country. Those with status granted before arrival in the receiving country include resettled refugees, and those who were living abroad at the time of application and whose application for permanent residence was considered concurrently with that of the protected person already living in the country. Refugee status can be granted on the basis of the 1951 Convention and the 1967 Protocol or pertinent regional instruments. The group may also include persons who qualify as refugees under national legal systems. Only refugees under the UNHCR mandate are covered here
